title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck showed that a free rank-2 module M over Λ = Z/4Z is equivalent to a triple (M_0, I_M, S_M). Here M_0 = M/2M is a 2-dimensional F_2-space, I_M is an M_0-torsor and S_M is a torsor under F_2^ω, the 2-dimensional F_2-space on the 2-element set ω. This comes from splitting the End(M_0)-torsor of lifts as End(M_0) ≅ M_0 ⊕ F_2^ω as GL(M_0) ≅ S_3-modules. This page translates that algebraic data into pure combinatorics.

Step 1. By §1, a pair (M_0, I) with I an M_0-torsor is the same thing as a bare 4-element set I.
- M_0 is recovered as V_I, the Klein four-group of double transpositions with the identity, acting simply transitively on I.
- M_0^* is recovered as P̃_{2,2}(I): the three partitions of I into two pairs, together with 0.
- Hence GL(M_0) ≅ S_3 = S_4/V_4, and Aut(M_0, I) = AGL(2, F_2) ≅ S_I.
- The 2-element set ω attached to M_0 becomes ω(I), the set of the two orientations of I (A_4-orbits of orderings). S_I acts on ω(I) through the sign.

Step 2. A 2-element set C together with a torsor S under F_2^C (the transcription's 'forme' should read 'torseur') is the same as a combinatorial square Q.
- S is the vertex set of Q.
- The two nonzero 'axis' translations of F_2^C move vertices along the two classes of opposite sides. C is the set of these classes; Grothendieck calls them 'codiagonales'.
- Aut(C, S) = F_2^C ⋊ S_2 = D_4 = D_Q, of order 8. χ_C : D_Q → {±1} is its action on C.

Step 3. The extra datum identifying the 2-element set ω(M_0) with C becomes a bijection k : ω(I) ≅ C(Q). This is formula (20).

Corollary 2, formula (21). There is a canonical equivalence of groupoids between free rank-2 Λ-modules and triples (I, Q, k), where I has 4 elements, Q is a combinatorial square and k : ω(I) ≅ C(Q).

Corollary 3, formula (22). Taking automorphism groups gives a cartesian square GL_Λ(M) = S_I ×_{±1} D_Q, fibred over sg : S_I → {±1} and χ_C : D_Q → {±1}.

Order check: 24·8/2 = 96 = |GL(2, Z/4)|, since |GL(2, F_2)| = 6 and the congruence kernel 1 + 2M_2(F_2) has order 16.

Consistency checks with the next page:
- The kernel of GL → D_Q is A_4 (order 12).
- The kernel of GL → S_I is ker χ_C (order 4).
- det is the composite GL → D_Q → {±1} given by the rotation character.
- Hence SL(2, Z/4) ≅ S_4 ×_{C_2} C_4. Its kernel to S_4 is {±1}, which recovers PSL(2, Z/4) ≅ S_4 (the octahedral group of X(4)). It also gives SL(2, Z/4)^ab ≅ Z/4, matching the known abelianization (SL(2, Z)^ab = Z/12 → Z/4).

Purpose: in a manuscript on moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2, this gives a canonical, choice-free combinatorial model of level-4 structures E[4]. It makes the quotients of GL(2, Z/4) onto S_4, D_4, S_3 and {±1} visible as automorphisms of a 4-set and a square.
errors: Minor wording: 'une forme S sur F_2^C' must mean a torsor S under F_2^C, not a form.

'Codiagonales' of Q must denote the two classes of opposite sides (the translation axes of the F_2^C-torsor), not the diagonals. The diagonals correspond to the sum vector (1,1). This is terminological, not a mathematical error.
Otherwise the statements check out: orders match (96), and the induced descriptions of SL(2, Z/4), PSL(2, Z/4) ≅ S_4 and SL^ab ≅ Z/4 are correct.

ideas.what: A 2-dim F_2-space together with a torsor under it is equivalent to a 4-element set (M_0 = V_I, M_0^* = 2+2 partitions)
ideas.modern_name: AGL(2, F_2) ≅ S_4; Klein four-group as translation group of the affine plane over F_2

ideas.what: A torsor under F_2^C (with |C| = 2) is equivalent to a combinatorial square, with automorphism group D_4
ideas.modern_name: D_4 = (Z/2)^2 ⋊ Z/2, symmetries of a square

ideas.what: Canonical equivalence of groupoids: free rank-2 Z/4-modules ↔ triples (I, Q, k), with I a 4-set, Q a square and k a bijection between orientations of I and 'codiagonals' of Q
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial model of the groupoid of rank-2 Z/4-modules; level-4 structures on elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard attribution known; the underlying group isomorphism is likely folklore

ideas.what: Cartesian square GL(2, Z/4) ≅ S_4 ×_{±1} D_4 (fibred over the sign and the codiagonal character), giving SL(2, Z/4) ≅ S_4 ×_{C_2} C_4
ideas.modern_name: structure of GL(2, Z/4Z) (SmallGroup of order 96) as a subdirect product of S_4 and D_4
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore / computational group theory; implicit in work on mod-4 Galois images of elliptic curves

missed.claim: The functorial combinatorial model makes the two canonical quotients of the mod-4 Galois representation of an elliptic curve explicit. The D_Q quotient (with det = rotation character) corresponds to the D_4 field Q(i, Δ^{1/4}). The S_I quotient is a canonical S_4-field attached to the 4-set I_{E[4]}, glued along the common quadratic subfield Q(√Δ). This is a canonical, choice-free description of the 4-torsion field as a fibre product, apparently in the spirit of anabelian / dessin combinatorics.
missed.quote: Corollaire 3 Si M est associé à I, Q, on a un diagramme cartésien canonique (22)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The group-theoretic fibre product is likely known computationally. A canonical groupoid-level model of level-4 structures (a 4-set plus a square plus a bijection) is a clean way to describe the moduli stack of level-4 structures and its intermediate covers (X(4) with S_4 symmetry, Δ^{1/4}). It does not seem to be written down in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct and elegant, but elementary. The group isomorphism GL(2, Z/4) ≅ S_4 ×_{C_2} D_4 is likely known to group theorists and in mod-4 elliptic-curve image work. The novelty is only the canonical groupoid-level combinatorial packaging (I, Q, k), which seems unrecorded but would not surprise a specialist much.
transcription_corrections: 'à la définition d'un ens. à deux éléments C, et d'une forme S sur F_2^C' should read roughly: 'la donnée d'un ens. à deux éléments C, et d'un torseur S sous F_2^C, équivaut à la donnée d'un carré Q'.
'Dans la groupoïde des données ... de (18)' likely reads 'Dans la groupoïde des données (M_0, I, S) de (18), [la donnée] est équivalente à celle des triples'.
In (22) the arrows are GL_Λ(M) → S_I and GL_Λ(M) → D_Q, with sg : S_I → {±1} and χ_C : D_Q → {±1}. χ_C is annotated '(opération sur l'ens. des codiagonales)'.
